Dictation

Choose the global hotkey. Hold to talk, or tap twice to start and stop.

Downloading speech model

Whisper large-v3-turbo (~1.5 GB) downloads once on first launch. Dictation works after this finishes.

Click here, then press keys…

macOS does not expose the Fn key to global shortcuts. If your combo is rejected, try F13 or Ctrl + Space. Side mouse buttons work well with tap-to-toggle.

Transcription

Where speech becomes text. Local runs fully offline (default).

Press Enter automatically after pasting (auto-send) Useful in chat apps when you want to send immediately after dictating.

Local keeps your voice on this Mac and needs no internet. Cloud backends send audio to a third party — faster and they free up ~1.5 GB of RAM, but require an API key and internet.

Display

Control the floating HUD pill and live transcript preview.

HUD
Keep HUD above other windows When off, the pill only floats up while you dictate.
Show live transcript while recording Preview words in the HUD before you release the hotkey.

Use reset for Classic or Notch if the pill disappears off-screen. Cursor style tracks your mouse while dictating.

Cleanup

Pick the local Ollama model used after rules cleanup. Rules always run first.

Ollama model

Type any Ollama model, or open the list to pick from installed ones. gemma3:1b is always available as the DictaFlow default.

Vocabulary

Teach DictaFlow names and terms to recognize, and corrections when Whisper gets them wrong.

Words to recognize

Names, brands, slang — comma-separated. Biases transcription before you dictate them.

Corrections

When Whisper hears one thing but you want another. Applied after transcription and fed back into future prompts.

Loading…

Corrections are learned automatically when you fix pasted text, or add them here manually. Ambiguous words like cloud are stored as phrases (e.g. “use cloud” → “use Claude”) so weather talk stays intact.

General

Open DictaFlow at login Keep the menu bar agent ready without launching the app manually.

Launch at login is not available in the Mac App Store build because of App Sandbox restrictions.

Permissions

DictaFlow needs Microphone, Accessibility, and Input Monitoring for dictation.

macOS access
Accessibility
Checking…
Input Monitoring
Checking…

First time: enable all three in System Settings. Click Request Accessibility, then toggle DictaFlow on for Accessibility and Input Monitoring. Microphone is prompted when you first dictate.
